nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:stable} 
For a numerical integrator $\overline{F}$ and $(x,v)\in\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}\times T_{x}\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}\times\mathbb{R}^{n}$, we call $\overline{F}$ \emph{sensitive} at $(x,v)$ if there exists step size $h_{0}(x,v)$ such that the numerical integrator with step size $h$ less than $h_{0}$ satisfies
\[
\frac{\Abs{D\overline{T}_{x,h}(v)}}{\Abs{DT_{x,h}(v')}}\geq0.998,
\]
where $v'$ satisfies $T_{x,h}(v')=\overline{T}_{x,h}(v)$ and the Jacobian $DT$ is taken with respect to the velocity variable. In other words, the solution of the numerical integrator changes almost as fast as the ideal solution does. Unless specified otherwise, a sensitive integrator is additionally assumed to be measure-preserving (i.e., $\det(D\overline{F}_h(x,v))=1$) and time-reversible (i.e., $\overline{F}_h(\overline{x}_h, -\overline{v}_h) = (x, -v)$).

In other words, the solution of the numerical integrator changes almost as fast as the ideal solution does. Unless specified otherwise, a sensitive integrator is additionally assumed to be measure-preserving (i.e., det(DoverlineF_h(x,v))=1) and time-reversible (i.e., overlineF_h(overlinex_h, -overlinev_h) = (x, -v)).

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{thm:discPoly} 
Let $\pi$ be a target distribution on a polytope with $m$ constraints
in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ such that $\frac{d\pi}{dx}\sim e^{-\alpha^{\top}x}$ for
$\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$. Let $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$ be the Hessian manifold of the polytope
induced by the logarithmic barrier of the polytope. Let $\Lambda=\sup_{S\subset\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}}\frac{\pi_{0}(S)}{\pi(S)}$
be the warmness of the initial distribution $\pi_{0}$. Let $\pi_{T}$
be the distribution obtained after $T$ steps of RHMC discretized
by a sensitive integrator on $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$. For any $\varepsilon>0$,
if for $x\in\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\frac{\varepsilon}{2\Lambda}}$ and $v\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ randomly
drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,g(x))$, we have that with probability at least
$0.99,$ step size $h\leq h_0(x,v)$,
\[
h\leq\frac{10^{-20}}{n^{7/12}\log^{1/2}\frac{\Lambda}{\varepsilon}},\ hC_{x}(x,v)\leq\frac{10^{-20}}{\sqrt{n}},\ h^{2}C_{x}(x,v)\leq\frac{10^{-10}}{n\log\frac{\Lambda}{\varepsilon}}\text{ and }h^{2}C_{v}(x,v)\leq\frac{10^{-10}}{\sqrt{n\log\frac{\Lambda}{\varepsilon}}},
\]
then $d_{\text{TV}}(\pi_{T},\pi)\leq\varepsilon$ for $T=O\Par{mh^{-2}\log\frac{\Lambda}{\varepsilon}}$.

For any varepsilon>0, if for xinM_fracvarepsilon2Lambda and vinR^n randomly drawn from N(0,g(x)), we have that with probability at least 0.99, step size hleq h_0(x,v), \[ hleqfrac10^-20n^7/12log^1/2fracLambdavarepsilon,\ hC_x(x,v)leqfrac10^-20sqrtn,\ h^2C_x(x,v)leqfrac10^-10nlogfracLambdavarepsilon and h^2C_v(x,v)leqfrac10^-10sqrtnlogfracLambdavarepsilon, \] then d_TV(pi_T,pi)leqvarepsilon for T=OParmh^-2logfracLambdavarepsilon.

nodes.raw_latex:
Consider a Markov chain with a state space $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$,
a transition distribution $\mathbb{\mathcal{T}}_{x}$ and stationary distribution
$\pi$. For any $s\in[0,1/2)$, the $s$-\emph{conductance} of the
Markov chain is 
\[
\Phi_{s}\stackrel{\mathrm{{\scriptscriptstyle def}}}{=}\inf_{\pi(S)\in(s,1-s)}\frac{\int_{S}\mathbb{\mathcal{T}}_{x}(S^{c})\pi(x)dx}{\min(\pi(S)-s,\pi(S^{c})-s)}.
\]

nodes.raw_latex:
Let $(\mathbb{\mathcal{M}},g)$ be a Riemannian manifold and $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}'$ a measurable subset of $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$ with $\pi(\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}')>\frac{1}{2}$.
The \emph{isoperimetry} $\psi$ of the subset with stationary distribution
$\pi$ is defined by 
\[
\psi_{\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}'}=\inf_{S\subset\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}'}\frac{\lim_{\delta\to0^{+}}\frac{1}{\delta}\int_{\{x\in\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}'\,:\,0<d_{g}(S,x)\leq\delta\}}\pi(x)dx}{\min(\pi(S),\pi(\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}'\backslash S))}.
\]

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{prop:conductance} For a Riemannian manifold $(\mathbb{\mathcal{M}},g)$,
let $\pi$ be the stationary distribution of a reversible Markov chain
on $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$ with a transition distribution $\mathbb{\mathcal{T}}_{x}$. Let $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}'\subset\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$
be a subset with $\pi(\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}')\geq1-\rho$ for some $\rho<\frac{1}{2}$.
We assume the following one-step coupling: if $d_{g}(x,x')\leq\Delta\leq1$
for $x,x'\in\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}'$, then $d_{\text{TV}}(\mathbb{\mathcal{T}}_{x},\mathbb{\mathcal{T}}_{x'})\leq0.9$. Then
for any $\rho\leq s<\frac{1}{2}$, the $s$-conductance is bounded
below by 
\[
\Phi_{s}\geq\Omega\Par{\psi_{\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}'}\Delta}.
\]

\label{def:auxiliary} An auxiliary function $\ell$ with parameters
$\ell_{0}$ and $\ell_{1}$ is a function that assigns a non-negative
real value to any Hamiltonian curve with step size $h$, such that 
\begin{itemize}
\item For any $x\in\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}$, we have 
\[
\mathbf{P}_{\gamma}\Par{\ell(\gamma)>\frac{1}{2}\ell_{0}}<\frac{1}{100}\min\Par{1,\frac{\ell_{0}}{\ell_{1}h}},
\]
where $\gamma$ is a Hamiltonian trajectory starting at $x$ with
an initial random velocity drawn from $\mathcal{N}(0,g(x)^{-1})$.
\item For any variations $\gamma_{s}$ starting from $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}$ with
$\ell(\gamma_{s})\leq\ell_{0}$, we have 
\[
\Abs{\frac{d}{ds}\ell(\gamma_{s})}\leq\ell_{1}\cdot\Par{\norm{\frac{d}{ds}\gamma_{s}(0)}_{\gamma_{s}(0)}+\delta\norm{D_{s}\gamma_{s}'(0)}_{\gamma_{s}(0)}},
\]
where the variations $\gamma_{s}$ satisfy the Hamiltonian equations,
and $D_{s}$ denotes the covariant derivative of the velocity field
$\gamma_{s}'(0)$ along a curve of starting points of the variations.
\end{itemize}

The Riemannian curvature tensor is a map $R:V(\mathbb{\mathcal{M}})\times V(\mathbb{\mathcal{M}})\times V(\mathbb{\mathcal{M}})\to V(\mathbb{\mathcal{M}})$
for $V(\mathbb{\mathcal{M}})$, the collection of vector fields on $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$, defined
by
\[
R(u,v)w=\nabla_{u}\nabla_{v}w-\nabla_{v}\nabla_{u}w-\nabla_{[u,v]}w\quad\text{for }u,v,w\in V(\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}),
\]
where $\nabla$ is the Levi-Civita connection on $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$, and $[u,v]\stackrel{\mathrm{{\scriptscriptstyle def}}}{=}\nabla_{u}v-\nabla_{v}u$
is the Lie bracket of the vector fields $u$ and $v$.

\label{def:smoothness} Given an auxiliary function $\ell$ with parameters
$\ell_{0}$ and $\ell_{1}$ and the operator $\Phi(\gamma,t):V(\mathbb{\mathcal{M}})\to V(\mathbb{\mathcal{M}})$
defined by $\Phi(\gamma,t)u\stackrel{\mathrm{{\scriptscriptstyle def}}}{=} D_{u}\mu(\gamma(t))-R(u,\gamma'(t))\gamma'(t)$, 
\begin{itemize}
\item $R_{1}$ is a parameter such that for any $t\in[0,h]$ and any Hamiltonian
curves $\gamma$ starting from $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}$ with step size $h$
and $\ell(\gamma)\leq\ell_{0}$ 
\[
\norm{\Phi(\gamma,t)}_{F,\gamma(t)}\stackrel{\mathrm{{\scriptscriptstyle def}}}{=}\sqrt{\mathbb{E}_{v,w\sim\mathcal{N}(0,g(\gamma(t))^{-1})}\inner{v,\Phi(\gamma,t)w}_{g(\gamma(t))}^{2}}\leq R_{1}.
\]
\item $R_{2}$ is a parameter such that for any $t\in[0,h]$, any Hamiltonian
curves $\gamma$ starting from $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}$ with step size $h$
and $\ell(\gamma)\leq\ell_{0}$, any curve $c(s)$ starting from $\gamma(t)$
and any vector field $v(s)$ along the curve $c(s)$ with $v(0)=\gamma'(t)$,
\[
\Abs{\frac{d}{ds}\mathrm{Tr}\Phi(v(s))\bigg\vert_{s=0}}\leq R_{2}\cdot\Par{\norm{\frac{dc}{ds}\bigg\vert_{s=0}}_{\gamma(t)}+h\norm{D_{s}v(s)\vert_{s=0}}_{\gamma(t)}},
\]
 where $v(s)$ in $\Phi$ indicates a Hamiltonian curve at time $t$
starting with an initial condition $(c(s),v(s))$.
\item $R_{3}$ is a parameter such that for any Hamiltonian curves $\gamma$
starting from $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}$ with step size $h$ and $\ell(\gamma)\leq\ell_{0}$,
if $\zeta(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$ is the parallel transport of
the vector $\gamma'(0)$ along $\gamma$, then 
\[
\sup_{t\in[0,h]}\norm{\Phi(\gamma,t)\zeta(t)}_{\gamma(t)}\leq R_{3}.
\]
\end{itemize}

\label{prop:idealConv}
Let $\pi_{T}$ be the distribution obtained after $T$ steps of a
lazy ideal RHMC with the stationary distribution $\pi$ satisfying
$\frac{d\pi}{dx}\sim e^{-f(x)}$. Let $\Lambda=\sup_{S\subset\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}}\frac{\pi_{0}(S)}{\pi(S)}$
be the warmness of an initial distribution $\pi_{0}$. For any $\varepsilon>0$,
let $\rho=\frac{\varepsilon}{2\Lambda}$ and $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}$ a good region.
If step size $h$ satisfies 
\[
h^{2}\leq\frac{1}{10^{10}R_{1}},\ h^{5}\leq\frac{\ell_{0}}{10^{3}R_{1}^{2}\ell_{1}},\ h^{3}R_{2}+h^{2}R_{3}\leq\frac{1}{10^{10}}\text{ and }h\leq\frac{1}{10^{10}}\min\Par{1,\frac{\ell_{0}}{\ell_{1}}},
\]
where the parameters are defined in Definition \ref{def:auxiliary}
and \ref{def:smoothness}, then for the isoperimetry $\psi_{\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}}$
of $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}$ there exists $T=O\Par{\Par{h\psi_{\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}}}^{-2}\log\frac{1}{\rho}}$
such that $d_{\text{TV}}(\pi_{T},\pi)\leq\varepsilon$.

implies that if $d_{\phi}(x,y)\lesssim h$, then $d_{\text{TV}}(\mathcal{P}_{x},\mathcal{P}_{y})\leq\frac{1}{1000}$.
By Proposition \ref{prop:conductance} with $\rho=s=\frac{\epsilon}{2\Lambda}$,
we can obtain the following lower bound on the $s$-conductance:
\[
\Phi_{s}=\Omega\Par{h\psi_{\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}}}.

By Lemma \ref{lem:tvDecrease}, we have

d_{\text{TV}}(\pi_{t},\pi)\leq s\Lambda+\Lambda\Par{1-\frac{\Phi_{s}^{2}}{2}}^{t}.
\]
Therefore, it suffices to choose $T=O\Par{\Par{h\psi_{\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}}}^{-2}\log\frac{1}{\rho}}$
to ensure $d_{\text{TV}}(\pi_{T},\pi)\leq\varepsilon$.

\label{thm:discGen} 
Let $\pi$ be a target distribution on a convex set $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$
and $\Lambda=\sup_{S\subset\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}}\frac{\pi_{0}(S)}{\pi(S)}$ be the
warmness of the initial distribution $\pi_{0}$. Let $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$ be the
Hessian manifold with its metric induced by the Hessian of a strongly
self-concordant barrier and $\pi_{T}$ the distribution obtained after
$T$ steps of RHMC discretized by a numerical integrator
on $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$. For any $\varepsilon>0$, let $\rho=\frac{\varepsilon}{2\Lambda}$
and $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}$ any good region. If step size $h$ guarantees
the sensitivity of the integrator and 
\begin{align*}
h^{2} & \leq\frac{10^{-10}}{\max(R_{1},\bar{R}_{1})},\ h^{5}\leq\frac{\ell_{0}}{10^{3}R_{1}^{2}\ell_{1}},\ h^{3}R_{2}+h^{2}R_{3}\leq1,\ h\leq\frac{1}{10^{10}}\min\Par{1,\frac{\ell_{0}}{\ell_{1}}},\ h^{2}\leq\frac{10^{-10}}{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}+M_{2}},\\
h & C_{x}(x,v)\leq\frac{10^{-10}}{\sqrt{n}},\ h^{2}C_{x}(x,v)\leq10^{-10}\min\Par{1,\frac{\bar{\ell}_{0}}{\bar{\ell}_{1}},\frac{1}{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}+\sqrt{M_{1}^{*}}}},\ h^{2}C_{v}(x,v)\leq\frac{10^{-10}}{\sqrt{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}}
\end{align*}
for $x\in\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}$ and $v\in V_{\text{good}}^{x}=\Brace{v\in\mathbb{R}^{n}:\norm v_{g^{-1}}\leq128\sqrt{n},\ \bar{\ell}(\mathrm{Ham}_{x,t}(g(x)^{-1}v))\leq\frac{1}{2}\bar{\ell}_{0}}$
(see (\ref{eq:vgood})), where the parameters are defined in Definition
\ref{def:auxiliary}, \ref{def:smoothness} and \ref{def:Mparameters},
then for the isoperimetry $\psi_{\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}}$ of $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}$
there exists $T=O\Par{\Par{h\psi_{\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}}}^{-2}\log\frac{1}{\rho}}$
such that $d_{\text{TV}}(\pi_{T},\pi)\leq\varepsilon$.

\label{lem:sc_facts} Let $g(x)=\nabla^{2}\phi(x)$ for some highly
self-concordant barrier $\phi$.
\begin{itemize}
\item $(1-\|y-x\|_{g(x)})^{2}g(x)\preceq g(y)\preceq\frac{1}{(1-\|y-x\|_{g(x)})^{2}}g(x).$ 
\item $\|Dg(x)[v,v]\|_{g(x)^{-1}}\leq2\|v\|_{g(x)}^{2}.$ 
\item $\|Dg(x)[v,v]-Dg(y)[v,v]\|_{g(x)^{-1}}\leq\frac{6}{(1-\|y-x\|_{g(x)})^{3}}\|v\|_{g(x)}^{2}\|y-x\|_{g(x)}.$

The first fact follows from Theorem 4.1.6 in \cite{nesterov2003introductory}.
The second fact follows from Lemma 4.1.2 in \cite{nesterov2003introductory}.
To be precise, 
\[
\norm{Dg(x)[v,v]}_{g(x)^{-1}}=\max_{\norm v_{g(x)}=1}Dg(x)[v,v,u]\leq2\norm v_{g(x)}^{2}.
\]

The third fact is from the following calculation: 
\begin{align*}
 & \|Dg(y)[v,v]-Dg(x)[v,v]\|_{g(x)^{-1}}\\
\leq & \int_{0}^{1}\|D^{2}g(x+t(y-x))[v,v,y-x]\|_{g(x)^{-1}}dt\\
\leq & \int_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{1-t\|y-x\|_{g(x)}}\|D^{2}g(x+t(y-x))[v,v,y-x]\|_{g(x+t(y-x))^{-1}}dt\\
\leq & \int_{0}^{1}\frac{6}{1-t\|y-x\|_{g(x)}}\|v\|_{g(x+t(y-x))}^{2}\|y-x\|_{g(x+t(y-x))}dt\\
\leq & \int_{0}^{1}\frac{6}{(1-t\|y-x\|_{g(x)})^{4}}dt\cdot\|v\|_{g(x)}^{2}\|y-x\|_{g(x)}\\
\leq & \frac{6}{(1-\|y-x\|_{g(x)})^{3}}\|v\|_{g(x)}^{2}\|y-x\|_{g(x)}.
\end{align*}
where the third and fifth line above follow from the first fact, and
the fourth line follows from Proposition 9.1.1 in \cite{nesterov1994interior}.

The fourth fact is from the following calculation:

= & \max_{\norm u_{g(x)}=1}Dg(x)[v,v,u]-Dg(x)[w,w,u]\\
= & \max_{\norm u_{g(x)}=1}Dg(x)[v-w,v,u]+Dg(x)[w,v-w,u]\\
= & \max_{\norm u_{g(x)}=1}Dg(x)[v-w,v,u]+Dg(x)[v-w,w,u]\\

\leq & 2\norm{v-w}_{g(x)}\norm{v+w}_{g(x)}.
\end{align*}

nodes.raw_latex:
To see this, let $V_{\text{bad}}^{x}$ be a set of bad initial
velocities of measure $\varepsilon<1$ and $V_{\text{good}}^{x}$ be the rest.
Assuming a one-to-one correspondence between $v$ and $v^{*}$ for
$v\in V_{\text{good}}^{x}$, we have that for $x\in\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}$
\begin{align*}
d_{\text{TV}}(\overline{\mathcal{P}}_{x},\mathcal{P}_{x}) & =\sup_{A\subset\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}}\int_{A}(\overline{p}_{x}(z)-p_{x}(z))dz\\
 & \leq\sup_{A\subset\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}}\int_{A}\Par{\sum_{v:\overline{T}_{x}(v)=z}\frac{p_{x}^{\ast}(v)}{\Abs{D\overline{T}_{x}(v)}}-\sum_{v^{*}:T_{x}(v^{*})=z}\frac{p_{x}^{\ast}(v^{*})}{\Abs{DT_{x}(v^{*})}}}dz\\
 & \leq\int_{V_{\text{bad}}^{x}}p_{x}^{*}(v)dv+\sup_{A\subset\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}}\int_{A}\sum_{v\in V_{\text{good}}^{x}:\overline{T}_{x}(v)=z}\Par{\frac{p_{x}^{\ast}(v)}{\Abs{D\overline{T}_{x}(v)}}-\frac{p_{x}^{\ast}(v^{*})}{\Abs{DT_{x}(v^{*})}}}dz\\
 & =P_{x}^{\ast}(V_{\text{bad}}^{x})+\sup_{A\subset\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}}\int_{A}\sum_{v\in V_{\text{good}}^{x}:\overline{T}_{x}(v)=z}\frac{p_{x}^{\ast}(v)}{\Abs{D\overline{T}_{x}(v)}}\Par{1-\frac{p_{x}^{\ast}(v^{*})}{p_{x}^{\ast}(v)}\frac{\Abs{D\overline{T}_{x}(v)}}{\Abs{DT_{x}(v^{*})}}}dz,
\end{align*}
where $P_{x}^{\ast}$ is $\mathcal{N}(0,g(x))$, and in the third line we
used the one-to-one correspondence between $v$ and $v^{*}$ to pair
them in the summation. If we show that on $v\in V_{\text{good}}^{x}$ the term of
$1-\frac{p_{x}^{\ast}(v^{*})}{p_{x}^{\ast}(v)}\frac{\Abs{D\overline{T}_{x}(v)}}{\Abs{DT_{x}(v^{*})}}$
is bounded by a small constant (say, $\eta$), then 
\begin{align*}
d_{\text{TV}}(\overline{\mathcal{P}}_{x},\mathcal{P}_{x}) & \leq P_{x}^{\ast}(V_{\text{bad}}^{x})+\eta\sup_{A\subset\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}}\int_{A}\sum_{v\in V_{\text{good}}^{x}:\overline{T}_{x}(v)=z}\frac{p_{x}^{\ast}(v)}{\Abs{D\overline{T}_{x}(v)}}dz\\
 & \leq P_{x}^{\ast}(V_{\text{bad}}^{x})+\eta\int_{V_{\text{good}}^{x}}p_{x}^{\ast}(v)dv\\
 & =P_{x}^{\ast}(V_{\text{bad}}^{x})+\eta P_{x}^{\ast}(V_{\text{good}}^{x})\\
 & \leq\eta+(1-\eta)\varepsilon.
\end{align*}
By taking $\varepsilon$ sufficiently small, we can bound
$d_{\text{TV}}(\overline{\mathcal{P}}_{x},\mathcal{P}_{x})$ smaller then $1/10$.

. For $0\leq t\leq h$, let us define $\phi(t):=\norm{x-x_{t}}_{g}$
and $\psi(t):=\norm{v-v_{t}}_{g^{-1}}$. Note that 
\begin{align*}
2\norm{x-x_{t}}_{g}\frac{d\phi(t)}{dt} & =\frac{d\phi^{2}(t)}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(x_{t}-x)^{\top}g(x_{t}-x)\\
 & =2\Par{\frac{\partial H}{\partial v}(x_{t},v_{t})}^{\top}g(x_{t}-x).
\end{align*}
Hence, 
\[
\Abs{\norm{x-x_{t}}_{g}\phi'(t)}=\Abs{\Par{\frac{\partial H}{\partial v}(x_{t},v_{t})}^{\top}g(x_{t}-x)}\leq\norm{\frac{\partial H}{\partial v}(x_{t},v_{t})}_{g}\norm{x_{t}-x}_{g},
\]
and $|\phi'(t)|\leq\norm{\frac{\partial H}{\partial v}(x_{t},v_{t})}_{g}$.
When $\norm{x-x_{t}}_{g}<\frac{1}{4}$ for $0\leq t\leq h$, since
the local norms at $x$ and $x_{t}$ are within a small constant factor
as follows, we have 
\begin{align*}
\norm{\frac{\partial H}{\partial v}(x_{t},v_{t})}_{g} & \leq2\norm{\frac{\partial H}{\partial v}(x_{t},v_{t})}_{g_{t}}=2\norm{v_{t}}_{g_{t}^{-1}}\quad(\text{Lemma \ref{lem:partH_dist}})\\
 & \leq4\norm{v_{t}}_{g^{-1}}\leq4(\norm{v_{t}-v}_{g^{-1}}+\norm v_{g^{-1}}),
\end{align*}
and thus 
\begin{equation}
\phi'(t)\leq10^{3}\sqrt{n}+4\psi(t)\quad\text{if }\norm{x-x_{t}}_{g}<\frac{1}{4}.\label{ineq1}
\end{equation}
Similarly, we can obtain 
\begin{align*}
2\norm{v-v_{t}}_{g^{-1}}\frac{d\psi}{dt} & =\frac{d\psi^{2}(t)}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(v_{t}-v)^{\top}g^{-1}(v_{t}-v)\\
 & =-2\Par{\frac{\partial H}{\partial x}(x_{t},v_{t})}^{\top}g^{-1}(v_{t}-v),
\end{align*}
and thus $|\psi'(t)|\leq\norm{\frac{\partial H}{\partial x}(x_{t},v_{t})}_{g^{-1}}$.
If $\norm{x-x_{t}}_{g}<\frac{1}{4}$ for $0\leq t\leq h$, then by
Lemma \ref{lem:partH_dist} 
\begin{align*}
\norm{\frac{\partial H}{\partial x}(x_{t},v_{t})}_{g^{-1}} & \leq2(\norm{v_{t}}_{g_{t}^{-1}}^{2}+\sqrt{M_{1}}+n)\quad(\because x\in\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho})\\
 & \leq2\Par{4\norm{v_{t}}_{g^{-1}}^{2}+\sqrt{M_{1}}+n}\\
 & \leq2\Par{8(\norm v_{g^{-1}}^{2}+\norm{v_{t}-v}_{g^{-1}}^{2})+\sqrt{M_{1}}+n}\quad(\because(a+b)^{2}\leq2(a^{2}+b^{2}))\\
 & \leq10^{6}n+16\psi^{2}(t)+2\sqrt{M_{1}},
\end{align*}
and thus 
\begin{equation}
\psi'(t)\leq10^{6}n+16\psi^{2}(t)+2\sqrt{M_{1}}\quad\text{if }\norm{x-x_{t}}_{g}<\frac{1}{4}.\label{ineq2}
\end{equation}
Now let us solve the coupled inequalities (\ref{ineq1}) and (\ref{ineq2}).
When $\psi(t)\leq1000t(n+\sqrt{M_{1}})$, (\ref{ineq2}) becomes 
\[
\psi'(t)\leq10^{6}n+2\sqrt{M_{1}}+16\cdot10^{6}t^{2}(n+\sqrt{M_{1}})^{2},
\]
and this inequality holds up until $h$ satisfying $\int_{0}^{h}\Par{10^{6}n+2\sqrt{M_{1}}+16\cdot10^{6}t^{2}(n+\sqrt{M_{1}})^{2}}dt\leq1000h(n+\sqrt{M_{1}})$.
We can check that for any $h\leq\frac{10^{-10}}{\sqrt{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}}$
(i.e., condition $\textcircled{\small{1}}$) this integral inequality is satisfied.
Recall that we have to ensure that $\phi(t)<\frac{1}{4}$ for $t\leq h$.
By substituting $\psi(t)\leq1000t(n+\sqrt{M_{1}})$ into (\ref{ineq1}),
we have 
\[
\phi'(t)\leq10^{3}\sqrt{n}+4000t(n+\sqrt{M_{1}}),
\]
as long as $\phi(t)=\norm{x_{t}-x}_{g}<\frac{1}{4}$. It is straightforward
to see that for $t\leq h$ one has 
\begin{align*}
\phi(t) & \leq10^{3}\sqrt{n}t+2000t^{2}(n+\sqrt{M_{1}})\leq10^{-7}\sqrt{\frac{n}{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}}+\frac{2000}{10^{10}}\\
 & <\frac{1}{10^{6}}.
\end{align*}

For $\delta_{x}=\norm{x_{t}-x_{t}'}_{g_{t}}$ and $\delta_{v}=\norm{v_{t}-v_{t}'}_{g_{t}^{-1}}$,
\begin{align*}

 & \leq\norm{v-v'}_{g_{t}^{-1}}+O(h)\sup_{t\in[0,h]}\Par{(\delta_{v}+\delta_{x}\norm{v_{t}}_{g^{-1}})(\norm{v_{t}}_{g^{-1}}+\norm{v_{t}'}_{g^{-1}})+(n+M_{2})\delta_{x}},

Let $z=\overline{T}_{x}(v)$ for $v\in V_{\text{good}}^{x}$. We show that
the map defined on $u\in V_{\text{dom}}=\{v'\in\mathbb{R}^{n}:\norm{v-v'}_{g^{-1}}\leq4\sqrt{n}\}$
by 
\[
\Upsilon(u)=u-\frac{1}{h}gT_{x}(u)+\frac{1}{h}gz,
\]
is Lipschitz in $u$ with respect to the local norm $g^{-1}$, and
then apply the Banach fixed-point theorem to obtain the unique fixed-point
$v^{*}$. Note that it satisfies $g(T_{x}(v^{*})-\overline{T}_{x}(v))=0$ and thus
$T_{x}(v^{*})=\overline{T}_{x}(v)$.

For Lipschitzness, let $(x_{t},u_{t})$ and $(x_{t}',u_{t}')$ be
the Hamiltonian curves of the ideal RHMC starting from $(x,u)$ and
$(x,u')$ for $u,u'\in V_{\text{dom}}$, respectively. Observe that
\begin{align}
 & \norm{\Upsilon(u)-\Upsilon(u')}_{g^{-1}}=\norm{u-u'-\frac{1}{h}g\Par{T_{x}(u)-T_{x}(u')}}_{g^{-1}}\label{eq:repeat}\\
 & =\norm{u-u'-\frac{1}{h}\int_{0}^{h}g\Par{g_{t}^{-1}u_{t}-g_{t}^{-1}u_{t}'}dt}_{g^{-1}}\nonumber \\
 & =\norm{\Par{I-\frac{1}{h}g\int_{0}^{h}g_{t}^{-1}dt}u-\Par{I-\frac{1}{h}g\int_{0}^{h}g_{t}'^{-1}dt}u'-\frac{1}{h}\int_{0}^{h}g\Par{\Gamma_{t}(u)-\Gamma_{t}(u')}dt}_{g^{-1}}\nonumber \\
 & =\norm{\underbrace{\frac{1}{h}\Par{\int_{0}^{h}(I-gg_{t}^{-1})dt}}_{I_{u}}u-\underbrace{\frac{1}{h}\Par{\int_{0}^{h}(I-gg_{t}'^{-1})dt}}_{I_{u'}}u'-\frac{1}{h}\int_{0}^{h}g\Par{\Gamma_{t}(u)-\Gamma_{t}(u')}dt}_{g^{-1}}\nonumber \\
 & \leq\norm{I_{u}(u-u')+(I_{u}-I_{u'})u'}_{g^{-1}}+\frac{1}{h}\norm{\int_{0}^{h}g\Par{\Gamma_{t}(u)-\Gamma_{t}(u')}dt}_{g^{-1}}\nonumber \\
 & \leq\norm{I_{u}(u-u')}_{g^{-1}}+\norm{(I_{u}-I_{u'})u'}_{g^{-1}}+\sup_{t\in[0,h]}\norm{\Gamma_{t}(u)-\Gamma_{t}(u')}_{g}\nonumber \\
 & \leq\underbrace{\norm{I_{u}(u-u')}_{g^{-1}}}_{F}+\underbrace{\norm{(I_{u}-I_{u'})u'}_{g^{-1}}}_{S}+L\norm{u-u'}_{g^{-1}},\label{eq:lastbound}
\end{align}
where the last inequality follows from the fourth item.

For $F$, let $p=u-u'$ and observe that 
\begin{align*}
\norm{I_{u}p}_{g^{-1}} & \leq\frac{1}{h}\int_{0}^{h}\norm{(I-gg_{t}^{-1})p}_{g^{-1}}dt\leq\sup_{t\in[0,h]}\norm{(I-gg_{t}^{-1})p}_{g^{-1}}\\
 & \leq O(1)\sup_{t\in[0,h]}\norm{I-g^{\frac{1}{2}}g_{t}^{-1}g^{\frac{1}{2}}}_{2}\norm p_{g^{-1}}\leq O(1)\sup_{t\in[0,h]}\norm{x-x_{t}}_{g}\norm p_{g^{-1}}\\
 & \lesssim\Par{h\sqrt{n}+h^{2}\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}}\norm{u-u'}_{g^{-1}}.\quad(\text{First item})
\end{align*}

For $S$, we can bound it as follows:
\begin{align*}

 & \lesssim\phi\sqrt{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}\lesssim h\sqrt{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}\norm{u-u'}_{g^{-1}}.\quad(\text{Third item})
\end{align*}
Substituting the bounds on $F$ and $S$ into (\ref{eq:lastbound})
with a small constant in $h$ taken, we can conclude that 
\[
\norm{\Upsilon(u)-\Upsilon(u')}_{g^{-1}}<\frac{1}{3}\norm{u-u'}_{g^{-1}}.
\]

Next, we show that the image of $\Upsilon$ is included in $V_{\text{dom}}$.
For $u\in V_{\text{dom}}$,
\begin{align*}
\norm{\Upsilon(u)-v}_{g^{-1}} & =\ginvnorm{u-v-\frac{1}{h}g(T_{x}(u)-\overline{T}_{x}(v))}\\
 & =\ginvnorm{u-v-\frac{1}{h}g(T_{x}(u)-T_{x}(v))+\frac{1}{h}g(T_{x}(v)-\overline{T}_{x}(v))}\\
 & \leq\norm{u-v-\frac{1}{h}g(T_{x}(u)-T_{x}(v))}_{g^{-1}}+\frac{1}{h}\norm{T_{x}(v)-\overline{T}_{x}(v)}_{g}.
\end{align*}
Repeating the proof for the first item\footnote{For $u\in V_{\text{dom}}$, we might have $\norm u_{g^{-1}}\geq128\sqrt{n}$
though, it is still bounded above by $132\sqrt{n}$. The proofs of
the second to fifth items can be exactly reproduced for $V_{\text{relaxed}}\stackrel{\mathrm{{\scriptscriptstyle def}}}{=}\{v'\in\mathbb{R}^{n}:\norm{v'}_{g^{-1}}\leq132\sqrt{n}\}$,
leading to a similar conclusion like $\norm{\Upsilon(u)-\Upsilon(u')}_{g^{-1}}<(\frac{1}{3}+\epsilon)\norm{u-u'}_{g^{-1}}$
for a small constant $\epsilon>0$.} (see (\ref{eq:repeat})), we can bound the first term by $\frac{1}{2}\norm{u-v}_{g^{-1}}$
and thus by $2\sqrt{n}$, due to $u\in V_{\text{dom}}$. By Lemma
\ref{lem:dist_const} and $\textcircled{\small{4}}$, we can bound the second term
by 
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{h}\norm{T_{x}(v)-\overline{T}_{x}(v)}_{g} & \leq\frac{2}{h}d_{g}(T_{x}(v),\overline{T}_{x}(v))\leq\frac{2}{h}C_{x}(x,v)h^{2}\leq2\sqrt{n}.
\end{align*}
Putting them together, we obtain $\norm{\Upsilon(u)-v}_{g^{-1}}\leq4\sqrt{n}$.

By the Banach fixed-point theorem, there is a unique fixed point $v^{*}$
of $\Upsilon$ such that $T_{x}(v^{*})=\overline{T}_{x}(v)$ and 
\[
\norm{\Upsilon(v)-v^{*}}_{g^{-1}}<\frac{1}{3}\norm{v-v^{*}}_{g^{-1}}.
\]
Moreover, $\norm{\Upsilon(v)-v^{*}}_{g^{-1}}=\norm{v-v^{*}-\frac{1}{h}g(T_{x}(v)-z)}_{g^{-1}}\geq\norm{v-v^{*}}_{g^{-1}}-\frac{1}{h}\norm{T_{x}(v)-\overline{T}_{x}(v)}_{g}$.
Relating these two inequalities, we obtain 
\[
\norm{v-v^{*}}_{g^{-1}}\lesssim\frac{1}{h}\norm{T_{x}(v)-\overline{T}_{x}(v)}_{g^{-1}}.
\]

 We now show a one-to-one correspondence between $v\in V_{\text{good}}^{x}$ and
$v^{*}$. Let $F_{h}(x,v)=(x_{2},v_{2})$ and $F_{h}(x,v^{*})=(z,v')$.
By the reversibility of the Hamiltonian trajectories, we have a one-to-one
correspondence between $v^{*}$ and $v'$ in a sense that $F_{h}(x,v^{*})=(z,v')$
and $F_{h}(z,-v')=(x,-v^{*})$. Similarly, we also have a one-to-one
correspondence between $v$ and $v_{2}$. Thus, it suffices to show
a one-to-one correspondence between $v_{2}\in T_{x_{2}}\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$ and
$v'\in T_{z}\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$. 

Consider the straight line between $z$ and $x_{2}$. We have that
$\norm{z-x_{2}}_{g}=\norm{\overline{T}_{x}(v)-T_{x}(v)}_{g}\leq2C_{x}(x,v)h^{2}\leq10^{-9}\min\Par{1,\frac{\bar{\ell}_{0}}{\bar{\ell}_{1}}}$
by $\textcircled{\small{3}}$ and $\bar{\ell}(\mathrm{Ham}_{x_{2},h}(-g(x_{2})^{-1}v_{2}))=\bar{\ell}(\mathrm{Ham}_{x,h}(g(x)^{-1}v))\leq\bar{\ell}_{0}/2$
by the symmetry of $\bar{\ell}$. Due to $\textcircled{\small{2}}$, we can apply
Lemma \ref{lem:extendGeo} to $x_{2}$ with an initial velocity $-g(x_{2})^{-1}v_{2}$.
Thus, a one-to-one correspondence between $v'$ and $v_{2}$ follows,
and we also have that $\bar{\ell}_{0}\geq\bar{\ell}(\mathrm{Ham}_{z,h}(-g(z)^{-1}v'))=\bar{\ell}(\mathrm{Ham}_{x,h}(g(x)^{-1}v^{*})$.

By Proposition \ref{prop:dynamics}-5, there exists $v^{*}$ such
that $T_{x}(v^{*})=\overline{T}_{x}(v)$ and $\bar{\ell}(\mathrm{Ham}_{x,t}(g(x)^{-1}v^{*}))\leq\bar{\ell}_{0}$.
Let us estimate $\Abs{DT_{x}(v^{*})}$. Recall that $\mathrm{Ham}_{x,h}$ is
the Hamiltonian map from $T_{x}\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$ to $\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}$, where both spaces
are endowed with the local metric $g$. Even though $T_{x}$ has the
same domain and range, these spaces are endowed with the Euclidean
metric. Therefore, we can relate $T_{x}$ to $\mathrm{Ham}_{x,h}$ by 
\[
T_{x}(v^{*})=\Par{\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}\to\mathbb{R}^{n}}\circ\mathrm{Ham}_{x,h}\circ\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{R}^{n}\to T_{x}\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}}}(g(x)^{-1}v^{*}),
\]
where $\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}\to\mathbb{R}^{n}}$ is the embedding with transition of
metric from $g(x)$ to the Euclidean, and $\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{R}^{n}\to T_{x}\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}}$
is the embedding with transition of metric from the Euclidean to $g(x)$.
Note that we have to normalize $v^{*}$ by $g(x)^{-1}$ before $\mathrm{Ham}_{x,h}$
takes it as input. Using this formula and the chain rule, 
\begin{align*}
\Abs{DT_{x}(v^{*})} & =\Abs{D\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}\to\mathbb{R}^{n}}(x')}\Abs{D\mathrm{Ham}_{x,h}(g(x)^{-1}v^{*})}\Abs{D\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{R}^{n}\to T_{x}\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}}(g(x)^{-1}v^{*})}\\
 & \leq\Abs{g(x')}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\cdot h^{n}\Par{1+\frac{2}{1000}}\cdot\Abs{g(x)}^{-1}\cdot\Abs{g(x)}^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
 & =\frac{h^{n}}{\sqrt{\Abs{g(x')}\Abs{g(x)}}}\Par{1+\frac{2}{1000}},
\end{align*}
where we used Corollary \ref{lem:jacoIdeal} for $\bar{\ell}$ in
the second line. Hence, if $\Abs{D\overline{T}_{x}(v)}\geq\frac{(1-10^{-6})h^{n}}{\sqrt{\Abs{g(x')}\Abs{g(x)}}}$,
then 
\[
\frac{\Abs{D\overline{T}_{x}(v)}}{\Abs{DT_{x}(v^{*})}}\geq\frac{1-10^{-6}}{1+0.002}\geq0.998.
\]

\label{lem:LeapIMM-second} For $x\in\mathbb{\mathcal{M}}_{\rho}$ and $v\in V_{\text{good}}^{x}$,
let $g=g(x)$ and $h$ step size of IMM with $h^{2}\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}\leq10^{-10}$.
Let $(\overline{x},\overline{v})$ be the point obtained from RHMC
discretized by IMM with the step size $h$ and initial condition $(x,v)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\norm{x-\overline{x}}_{g}=O\Par{h\sqrt{n}+h^{2}\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}}$
and $\norm{v-\overline{v}}_{g^{-1}}=O\Par{h\Par{\norm{\nabla f(\bar{x})}_{g^{-1}}+n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}}$.
\item $C_{x}(x,v)=O\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}$.
\item $C_{v}(x,v)=O\Par{\sqrt{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}+M_{2}^{*}}}$
.
\end{enumerate}

Let $\overline{F}(x,v)=(\bar{x},\bar{v})$ and $\overline{T}_{x}(v)=\bar{x}$. We lower bound
$\Abs{D\overline{T}_{x}(v)}.$ Recall that one iteration of IMM consists of three
steps with input $(x,v)$ and output $(x_{1},v_{1})$, as described
in the following diagram: 
\[
\Par{x,v}\overset{X}{\longrightarrow}\Par{x_{\frac{1}{3}},v_{\frac{1}{3}}}\overset{Y}{\longrightarrow}\Par{x_{{\frac{2}{3} }},v_{{\frac{2}{3} }}}\overset{Z}{\longrightarrow}\Par{x_{1},v_{1}},
\]
where each of the maps $X,Y$ and $Z$ is defined by 
\begin{align*}
X\Par{x,v} & =\Par{x,v-\frac{h}{2}\frac{\partial H_{1}(x,v)}{\partial x}},\\
Y\Par{x_{\frac{1}{3}},v_{\frac{1}{3}}} & =\Par{x_{\frac{1}{3}}+h\frac{\partial H_{2}(x_{\mathrm{mid}},v_{\mathrm{mid}})}{\partial v},v_{\frac{1}{3}}-h\frac{\partial H_{2}(x_{\mathrm{mid}},v_{\mathrm{mid}})}{\partial x}},\\
Z\Par{x_{{\frac{2}{3} }},v_{{\frac{2}{3} }}} & =\Par{x_{{\frac{2}{3} }},v_{{\frac{2}{3} }}-\frac{h}{2}\frac{\partial H_{1}(x_{{\frac{2}{3} }},v_{{\frac{2}{3} }})}{\partial x}},
\end{align*}
for $x_{\mathrm{mid}}=\frac{x_{\frac{1}{3}}+x_{{\frac{2}{3} }}}{2}$ and $v_{\mathrm{mid}}=\frac{v_{\frac{1}{3}}+v_{{\frac{2}{3} }}}{2}$.
Due to $\overline{T}_{x}(v)=\pi_{x}\circ(Z\circ Y\circ X)(x,v)$, it follows that
$D\overline{T}_{x}(v)$ is the upper-right $n\times n$ submatrix of $D(Z\circ Y\circ X)(x,v)$.
From direct computation, we have 
\begin{align*}
DX(x,v) & =\left[\begin{array}{cc}
I & 0\\*
* & I
\end{array}\right],\\
DY(x_{\frac{1}{3}},v_{\frac{1}{3}}) & =\left[\begin{array}{cc}
P & Q\\
R & S
\end{array}\right],\\
DZ(x_{{\frac{2}{3} }},v_{{\frac{2}{3} }}) & =\left[\begin{array}{cc}
I & 0\\*
* & I
\end{array}\right],
\end{align*}
and due to $D(Z\circ Y\circ X)=DZ\cdot DY\cdot DX$ we have $D\overline{T}_{x}(v)=Q$.
Thus, it suffices to focus on the second step only (i.e., the map
$Y$).

Now let us represent the map $Y$ in a compact way. With two symbols
\[
r=\left[\begin{array}{c}
x\\
v
\end{array}\right]\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}\ \text{and}\ J=\left[\begin{array}{cc}
0 & I_{n}\\
-I_{n} & 0
\end{array}\right]\in\mathbb{R}^{2n\times2n},
\]
the second step can be rewritten as 
\[
r_{{\frac{2}{3} }}=r_{\frac{1}{3}}+hJ\nabla_{(x,v)}H_{2}(r_{\mathrm{mid}}),
\]
where $r_{*}=\left[\begin{array}{c}
x_{*}\\
v_{*}
\end{array}\right]$ for $*\in\Brace{\frac{1}{3},{\frac{2}{3} ,\mathrm{mid}}}$ and $H_{2}(x,v)=\frac{1}{2} v^{\top}g(x)^{-1}v$.
Differentiating both sides by $r_{\frac{1}{3}}$,
\[
\frac{\partial r_{{\frac{2}{3} }}}{\mathcal{\partial} r_{\frac{1}{3}}}=I_{2n}+hJ\nabla^{2}H_{2}(r_{\mathrm{mid}})\Par{\frac{1}{2} I_{2n}+\frac{1}{2}\frac{\partial r_{{\frac{2}{3} }}}{\mathcal{\partial} r_{\frac{1}{3}}}}.
\]
As $DY\Par{r_{\frac{1}{3}}}=\frac{\partial r_{{\frac{2}{3} }}}{\mathcal{\partial} r_{\frac{1}{3}}}$, we
have that
\[
\Par{I_{2n}-\frac{h}{2}J\nabla^{2}H_{2}(r_{\mathrm{mid}})}DY\Par{r_{\frac{1}{3}}}=I_{2n}+\frac{h}{2}J\nabla^{2}H_{2}(r_{\mathrm{mid}}).
\]
 For $G(x)\stackrel{\mathrm{{\scriptscriptstyle def}}}{=}\left[\begin{array}{cc}
g(x)^{\frac{1}{2}} & 0\\
0 & g(x)^{-\frac{1}{2}}
\end{array}\right]$, we have 
\begin{align*}
G(x_{\mathrm{mid}}) & \Par{I_{2n}-\frac{h}{2}J\nabla^{2}H_{2}(r_{\mathrm{mid}})}G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})DY\Par{r_{\frac{1}{3}}}G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}\\
 & =G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})\Par{I_{2n}+\frac{h}{2}J\nabla^{2}H_{2}(r_{\mathrm{mid}})}G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}
\end{align*}
and 
\begin{align}
 & \Par{I_{2n}-\frac{h}{2}G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})J\nabla^{2}H_{2}(r_{\mathrm{mid}})G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}}G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})DY\Par{r_{\frac{1}{3}}}G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}\nonumber \\
 & =I_{2n}+\frac{h}{2}G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})J\nabla^{2}H_{2}(r_{\mathrm{mid}})G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}.\label{eq:impdiff}
\end{align}
Let us look into the term $B\stackrel{\mathrm{{\scriptscriptstyle def}}}{=} G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})J\nabla^{2}H_{2}(r_{\mathrm{mid}})G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}$.
By direct computation, for block matrices $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3},B_{4}$
of size $n\times n$ we have
\begin{align*}
B & \stackrel{\mathrm{{\scriptscriptstyle def}}}{=}\left[\begin{array}{cc}
B_{1} & B_{2}\\
B_{3} & B_{4}
\end{array}\right]\\
 & =\left[\begin{array}{cc}
g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
 & g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}
\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{cc}
\frac{\mathcal{\partial}^{2}H_{2}}{\mathcal{\partial} v\mathcal{\partial} x}(r_{\mathrm{mid}}) & \frac{\mathcal{\partial}^{2}H_{2}}{\mathcal{\partial} v^{2}}(r_{\mathrm{mid}})\\
-\frac{\mathcal{\partial}^{2}H_{2}}{\mathcal{\partial} x^{2}}(r_{\mathrm{mid}}) & -\Par{\frac{\mathcal{\partial}^{2}H_{2}}{\mathcal{\partial} x\mathcal{\partial} v}(r_{\mathrm{mid}})}^{\top}
\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{cc}
g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}\\
 & g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{\frac{1}{2}}
\end{array}\right]
\end{align*}
and thus 
\begin{align}
B_{1} & =g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}Dg(x_{\mathrm{mid}})\Brack{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}}}g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}},\label{eq:LMIMM-eq4}\\
B_{2} & =I_{n},\nonumber \\
B_{3} & =g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}\bigg(-v_{\mathrm{mid}}^{\top}g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}Dg(x_{\mathrm{mid}})g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}Dg(x_{\mathrm{mid}})g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}}\nonumber \\
 & ~~+\frac{1}{2} v_{\mathrm{mid}}^{\top}g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}D^{2}g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}}\bigg)g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}\nonumber \\
 & =-B_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}D^{2}g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})\Brack{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}},g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}}}g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}},\nonumber \\
B_{4} & =-B_{1}^{\top}.\nonumber 
\end{align}
Now we bound the operator norm of $B_{i}$ for each $i\in[4]$ as
follows. 
\begin{align*}
\norm{B_{1}} & =\norm{B_{4}}\\
 & =\max_{p,q:\norm p_{2},\norm q_{2}\leq1}p^{\top}g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}Dg(x_{\mathrm{mid}})\Brack{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}}}g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}q\\
 & =\max_{p,q}Dg(y_{\mathrm{mid}})\Brack{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}},g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}p,g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}q}\\
 & \leq2\max_{p,q}\norm{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}}}_{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})}\norm{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}p}_{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})}\norm{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}q}_{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})}\\
 & =2\max_{p,q}\norm{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}}}_{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})}\norm p_{2}\norm q_{2}\leq2\norm{v_{\mathrm{mid}}}_{g_{\mathrm{mid}}^{-1}}\\
 & \leq O\Par{\sqrt{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}},
\end{align*}
where we used (\ref{eq:LMIMM-ineq4}) guaranteed by the condition
of $h^{2}\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}\leq10^{-10}$ ($\textcircled{\small{1}}$ in Proposition
\ref{prop:dynamics}). For $B_{2}$ and $B_{3}$, we have
\begin{align*}
\norm{B_{2}} & =1,\\
\norm{B_{3}} & \leq\norm{B_{1}}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}\max_{p,q:\norm p_{2},\norm q_{2}\leq1}D^{2}g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})\Brack{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}},g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}},g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}p,g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}q}\\
 & \leq O\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}+3\max_{p,q}\norm{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}}}_{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})}^{2}\norm{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}p}_{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})}\norm{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}q}_{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})}\\
 & =O\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}+O\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}\max_{p,q}\norm p_{2}\norm q_{2}\\
 & =O\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}},
\end{align*}
where the second inequality for $\norm{B_{3}}$ follows from the highly
self-concordance of $\phi$. Due to $\norm B\leq\sum_{i=1}^{4}\norm{B_{i}}$,
we have $\norm{\frac{h}{2}B}=O\Par{h\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}}$. Hence,
the condition of $h^{2}\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}^{2}\leq10^{-10}$ ensures
that the inverse of $I_{2n}-\frac{h}{2}B$ exists, and it can be written
as a series of matrices, 
\[
\Par{I_{2n}-\frac{h}{2}B}^{-1}=\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}(hB/2)^{i}.
\]
By substituting this series into (\ref{eq:impdiff}), 
\begin{align*}
G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})DY\Par{r_{\frac{1}{3}}}G(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1} & =\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}(hB/2)^{i}\Par{I_{2n}+\frac{h}{2}B}=\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}(hB/2)^{i}+\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}(hB/2)^{i}\\
 & =I_{2n}+2\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}(hB/2)^{i}.
\end{align*}
By multiplying $\left[\begin{array}{cc}
I_{n} & 0\end{array}\right]^{\top}$ to the left and $\left[\begin{array}{c}
0\\
I_{n}
\end{array}\right]$ to the right on both sides, 
\[
g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{\frac{1}{2}}D\overline{T}_{x}(v)g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{\frac{1}{2}}=2\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\left[\begin{array}{cc}
I_{n} & 0\end{array}\right]^{\top}(hB/2)^{i}\left[\begin{array}{c}
0\\
I_{n}
\end{array}\right].
\]
From (\ref{eq:LMIMM-eq4}), $B$ is of the form
\[
B=\left[\begin{array}{cc}
C & I_{n}\\
-C^{2}+R & -C
\end{array}\right],
\]
where $C\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is symmetric and $R\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$,
and thus by Lemma \ref{lem:matrixSeries}
\[
g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{\frac{1}{2}}D\overline{T}_{x}(v)g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{\frac{1}{2}}=h\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}(h^{2}R/2)^{i},
\]
where $R=\frac{1}{2} g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}D^{2}g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})\Brack{g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}},g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-1}v_{\mathrm{mid}}}g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{-\frac{1}{2}}$.
Thus for $E\stackrel{\mathrm{{\scriptscriptstyle def}}}{=}\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}(h^{2}R/2)^{i}$ 
\begin{equation}
\frac{1}{h}g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{\frac{1}{2}}D\overline{T}_{x}(v)g(x_{\mathrm{mid}})^{\frac{1}{2}}=I+E.\label{eq:LMIMM-last}
\end{equation}

We now bound its operator norm, trace and Frobenius norm. It is easy
to see that 
\begin{align*}
\norm E_{2} & \lesssim\sum_{i\geq1}\Par{\frac{h^{2}}{2}\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}}^{i},\\
\mathrm{Tr}(E) & \lesssim\sum_{i\geq1}\Par{\frac{h^{2}}{2}\mathrm{Tr}(R)}^{i}\leq\sum_{i\geq1}\Par{\frac{h^{2}}{2}n\Par{n+\sqrt{M_{1}}}},\\
\norm E_{F} & \lesssim\sum_{i\geq1}\Par{\frac{h^{2}}{2}\sqrt{n}\Par{n+\sqrt{M}}}^{i},
\end{align*}
where we used the following estimations

Let $\overline{T}_{x}(v)=\bar{x}=x_{1}$. We lower bound $\Abs{D\overline{T}_{x}(v)}$. It suffices
to look into the determinant of composition of first two steps in
Algorithm \ref{alg:LM}, since the third step only changes $v$. The
first two steps are 

\begin{align*}
v_{\frac{1}{2}} & =v-\frac{h}{2}\frac{\mathcal{\partial} H}{\mathcal{\partial} x}(x,v_{\frac{1}{2}}),\\
x_{1} & =x+\frac{h}{2}\Par{\frac{\mathcal{\partial} H}{\mathcal{\partial} v}(x,v_{\frac{1}{2}})+\frac{\mathcal{\partial} H}{\mathcal{\partial} v}(x_{1},v_{\frac{1}{2}})}.
\end{align*}
Differentiating the first equation with respect to $v$, we have 
\[
\frac{\mathcal{\partial} v_{\frac{1}{2}}}{\mathcal{\partial} v}=I_{n}-\frac{h}{2}\frac{\mathcal{\partial}^{2}H}{\mathcal{\partial} x\mathcal{\partial} v}\Par{x,v_{\frac{1}{2}}}\frac{\mathcal{\partial} v_{\frac{1}{2}}}{\mathcal{\partial} v},
\]
and so
\begin{equation}
\Par{I+\frac{h}{2}\frac{\mathcal{\partial}^{2}H}{\mathcal{\partial} x\mathcal{\partial} v}\Par{x,v_{\frac{1}{2}}}}\frac{\mathcal{\partial} v_{\frac{1}{2}}}{\mathcal{\partial} v}=I_{n}.\label{eq:step1diff}
\end{equation}
Differentiating the second equation with respect to $v$, we obtain
\[
\frac{\mathcal{\partial} x_{1}}{\mathcal{\partial} v}=\frac{h}{2}\Par{\frac{\mathcal{\partial}^{2}H}{\mathcal{\partial} v^{2}}\Par{x,v_{\frac{1}{2}}}\frac{\mathcal{\partial} v_{\frac{1}{2}}}{\mathcal{\partial} v}+\frac{\mathcal{\partial}^{2}H}{\mathcal{\partial} x\mathcal{\partial} v}\Par{x_{1},v_{\frac{1}{2}}}\frac{\mathcal{\partial} x_{1}}{\mathcal{\partial} v}+\frac{\mathcal{\partial}^{2}H}{\mathcal{\partial} v^{2}}\Par{x_{1},v_{\frac{1}{2}}}\frac{\mathcal{\partial} v_{\frac{1}{2}}}{\mathcal{\partial} v}}.
\]
Collecting all $\mathcal{\partial} x_{1}/\mathcal{\partial} v$ terms from this equation, for

For a convex body $\mathcal{K}$, the cross-ratio distance $d_{\mathcal{K}}(x,y)$
between $x$ and $y$ is 
\[
d_{\mathcal{K}}(x,y)=\frac{|x-y||p-q|}{|p-x||y-q|},
\]
where $p$ and $q$ are on the boundary of $\mathcal{K}$ such that $p,x,y,q$
are on the straight line $\overline{xy}$ and are in order. The Hilbert
distance $d_{H}$ between $x,y\in\mathcal{K}$ is 
\[
d_{H}(x,y)=\log(1+d_{\mathcal{K}}(x,y))=\log\Par{1+\frac{|x-y||p-q|}{|p-x||y-q|}}.
\]
For sets $X$ and $Y$, we define $d_{*}(X,Y)=\inf_{x\in X,y\in Y}d_{*}(x,y)$
for $*\in\{\mathcal{K},H,\phi\}$.

Let $\rho=\frac{\varepsilon}{2\Lambda}$. We first bound $M_{1},M_{1}^{*}$
by $20n^{2}\log^{2}\frac{1}{\rho}$ and set $M_{2}$ to $0$. Substituting
these to Lemma \ref{lem:l1}, \ref{lem:R1}, \ref{lem:R2} and \ref{lem:R3},
we have

R_{1} & \lesssim n\log\frac{1}{\rho},\\
R_{2} & \lesssim n^{3/2}\log\frac{1}{\rho}+h^{2}n^{5/2}\log^{2}\frac{1}{\rho}+\frac{\sqrt{n\log\frac{1}{\rho}}}{h}+\frac{\sqrt{n\log n}}{h},\\
R_{3} & \lesssim n\sqrt{\log n}\log\frac{1}{\rho}+hn^{7/4}\log^{3/2}\frac{1}{\rho}.

\label{def:sc-barrier} 
A self-concordant barrier $\phi:K\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a function such that $\phi(x)\to\infty$
as $x\to\mathcal{\partial} K$ and that $\Abs{Df^{3}(x)[h,h,h]}\leq2\Par{D^{2}f(x)[h,h]}^{3/2}$
for all $x\in K$ and $h\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$. If $\Abs{Df^{4}(x)[h,h,h,h]}\leq6\Par{D^{2}f(x)[h,h]}^{2}$
is also satisfied for all $h$, then $\phi$ is called a highly self-concordant
barrier.

If AbsDf^4(x)[h,h,h,h]leq6ParD^2f(x)[h,h]^2 is also satisfied for all h, then phi is called a highly self-concordant barrier.
nodes.label: def:sc-barrier

nodes.name: Riemannian length and distance
nodes.statement: Let phi:R^nrightarrowR be a self-concordant function. For all xinR^d, we define the local norm induced by nabla^2phi(x) by \[ norm h_nabla^2phi(x)=sqrth^topnabla^2phi(x)h. \] For any smooth curve c:[0,1]rightarrowR^n, we define the length of the curve as \[ L_phi(c)=int_0^1normfracddtc(t)_nabla^2phi(c(t))dt. \] For any x,yinR^d, we define the distance d_phi(x,y) to be the infimum of the lengths of all piecewise smooth curves with c(0)=x and c(1)=y.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:RiemannDistance} 
Let $\phi:\mathbb{R}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ be a self-concordant function. For all
$x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$, we define the local norm induced by $\nabla^{2}\phi(x)$
by 
\[
\norm h_{\nabla^{2}\phi(x)}=\sqrt{h^{\top}\nabla^{2}\phi(x)h}.
\]
For any smooth curve $c:[0,1]\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{n}$, we define the length
of the curve as 
\[
L_{\phi}(c)=\int_{0}^{1}\norm{\frac{d}{dt}c(t)}_{\nabla^{2}\phi(c(t))}dt.
\]
For any $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$, we define the distance $d_{\phi}(x,y)$ to
be the infimum of the lengths of all piecewise smooth curves with
$c(0)=x$ and $c(1)=y$.
